title: Todos the Physician
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Mishnah Bekhorot 4:4: an incident of a cow whose womb was removed; Rabbi Tarfon fed it to the dogs, and the case came before the sages (at Yavneh — Gemara), who permitted it. Todos the physician said: “No cow or sow leaves Alexandria without their cutting out its womb.”

In Nazir 52a and Tosefta Ohalot, chapter 4: an incident in which they brought a box full of bones to the synagogue of the Tarsians and set it in an open space; Todos the physician and all the physicians came in and said, “There is no spine of a single corpse here.” The incident is cited in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1, folio 6b, and there Rabbi Akiva was present.

notes.text: The supplied Berakhot chapter/halakhah/folio is Jerusalem Talmud. The spinal-column statement concerns bones attributed to one corpse, preserving the physicians’ quoted negative. The supplied פ:א is read as chapter1. “In an open space” does not add an unproved assertion that the synagogue was unroofed.
The physicians say that the bones do not contain the spine of one single corpse; they do not say that no spinal bones were present. “Open space” does not establish that the synagogue was unroofed.
